## 461d3a83ca9e

**Finding: all generated emitter-block examples use adjacent emitters, so a distance-specific blocker shortcut fits the complete generated sample.**

`_aligned_emitter_pairs` only uses diagonal distance 1. All other profiles draw opposite-parity emitter pairs, which cannot be diagonally aligned. Therefore the wrong rule “an emitter blocks a ray only when it is immediately adjacent; non-adjacent emitters are transparent” matched the official output on all 720 generated draws I checked (30 seeds × 8 sample indices × 3 bands). The 180 aligned draws all had emitter distance exactly 1.

A valid 9×9 counterexample with emitters separated by three diagonal steps is:

```text
000055500
000000000
002000000
000000000
000000000
000003000
000000000
000000000
000000000
```

The task's own `self_check` accepts this grid. Under the selected rule, cells `(0,0)` and `(1,1)` remain color 2 because the lower emitter's northwest ray stops at the upper emitter. The adjacent-only shortcut makes both cells color 3 by passing through the non-adjacent emitter. The exact official and shortcut outputs are recorded in `checks/audit_probes.json`.

A focused repair would add emitter-block profiles at multiple diagonal separations, including at least one case with painted cells before the blocker and visible cells beyond it. That would refute the shortcut without introducing ray-overlap ambiguity.
